# OOP Without Objects

The shapes problem again (see *Shapes in Three Type Systems*), but in a language that rejects the bundle-state-with-behaviour premise. Clojure splits the two:

- **Records** hold data. Immutable, comparable by value.
- **Protocols** hold behaviour. Like interfaces, but you can extend them to types you don't own — even years later.
- **Multimethods** dispatch on *anything*, not just the type of the first argument.

**Heads-up:** Clojure runs here as ClojureScript in your browser, so it starts instantly. In the DevTools Hub you can switch Clojure to the real JVM (Runtime center); this code works on both, using `#?(:clj … :cljs …)` where the two differ.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

(defprotocol Shape
  (area [s])
  (perimeter [s]))

(defrecord Circle [r]
  Shape
  (area [_] (* Math/PI r r))
  (perimeter [_] (* 2 Math/PI r)))

(defrecord Rect [w h]
  Shape
  (area [_] (* w h))
  (perimeter [_] (* 2 (+ w h))))

(defrecord Triangle [a b c]
  Shape
  (area [_]
    (let [s (/ (+ a b c) 2)]
      (Math/sqrt (* s (- s a) (- s b) (- s c)))))
  (perimeter [_] (+ a b c)))

(def shapes [(->Circle 2) (->Rect 3 4) (->Triangle 3 4 5)])

(doseq [s shapes]
  (println (format "%-25s area=%8.4f  perimeter=%8.4f"
                   (pr-str s) (double (area s)) (double (perimeter s)))))

;; Records are VALUES: equal by content, no identity headaches.
(println "value equality:" (= (->Rect 3 4) (->Rect 3 4)))

;; Protocols extend to types you don't own - here, plain strings
;; (area = the string's length, just to make the point):
(extend-protocol Shape
  #?(:clj String :cljs string)
  (area [s] (count s))
  (perimeter [s] (* 2 (count s))))
(println "a string can be a Shape now:" (area "hello"))

(def json
  (str/join ","
    (map (fn [s]
           (format "{\"name\":\"%s\",\"area\":%.4f}"
                   (-> s type str (str/split #"\.") last str/lower-case)
                   (double (area s))))
         shapes)))
(println (str "__NB_SET__ {\"key\":\"areas_clj\",\"value\":[" json "]}"))

## Multimethods: dispatch on anything

Protocols dispatch on the type of the first argument — same as Java. Multimethods dispatch on **any function of the arguments**, which covers cases OOP handles awkwardly (visitor pattern, double dispatch):

;; Dispatch on a KEY in a plain map - no records needed at all.
(defmulti describe :terrain)

(defmethod describe :mountain [m]
  (str "climb " (:name m) " at " (:height m) "m"))
(defmethod describe :river [m]
  (str "cross " (:name m) ", " (:length m) "km long"))
(defmethod describe :default [m]
  (str "wander around " (:name m)))

(doseq [place [{:terrain :mountain :name "Ben Nevis" :height 1345}
               {:terrain :river    :name "the Severn" :length 354}
               {:terrain :swamp    :name "the marshes"}]]
  (println (describe place)))

;; Double dispatch: collision handling by BOTH types - a pain with
;; classes and visitors, one line per case here.
(defmulti collide (fn [a b] [(:kind a) (:kind b)]))
(defmethod collide [:asteroid :ship] [_ _] "ship takes hull damage")
(defmethod collide [:ship :ship]     [_ _] "both ships bounce")
(defmethod collide :default          [_ _] "nothing happens")

(println (collide {:kind :asteroid} {:kind :ship}))
(println (collide {:kind :ship} {:kind :ship}))
(println (collide {:kind :asteroid} {:kind :asteroid}))

## The point

Java asks "what class is this object?" Clojure asks "what function handles this value?" — polymorphism becomes a lookup table you can extend from outside, and since records never mutate, the classic OOP puzzles about shared mutable state simply don't come up.

## Try this

- Add a `scale` method to the `Shape` protocol. Records are immutable — return a *new* record with `(->Circle (* 2 r))` or `(update s :r * 2)`.
- Extend `Shape` to numbers as well (`#?(:clj Number :cljs number)`): treat a number as the side of a square.
- Add a `[:ship :asteroid]` collision method — note you had to be explicit; multimethods don't assume symmetry.
